The test issues multiple complementary assertions (instance distinctness, vertex count preservation, and edge existence in both original and transposed graphs) verifying several properties of the result, not just a single superficial check.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods are present; the test is active and runnable (uses @Test(timeout=4000)).
The class Javadoc explicitly references requirement IDs (REQ-Graph-001, REQ-Graph-002, REQ-Graph-003), providing traceability between tests and requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses @Test(timeout = 4000), which is an explicit timing guard; per decision rules this counts as an explicit performance-related test annotation present in the test.
The method name is generic ('test8') and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (e.g., method_scenario_expectedResult). The name fails to communicate the scenario or expected outcome.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The class imports org.evosuite.runtime and the test name 'test8' plus the presence of Grafo_ESTest_scaffolding indicate EvoSuite-generated scaffolding and auto-generated style rather than minimal hand-written tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The method uses Given-When-Then comments and BDD-style structure in the test body and class Javadoc, indicating deliberate test design and intent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public Grafo APIs and does not use reflection or access internal private state; it verifies observable behavior through public methods.
Assertions include descriptive messages and use specific assertion methods (assertEquals, assertNotSame, assertTrue) rather than generic assertTrue only; messages improve diagnosability.
The test contains concise Given-When-Then comments and class-level Javadoc explaining requirements; there is no commented-out code or excessive inline comments.
The test does not use random values, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external resources; it uses deterministic local state and no sources of non-determinism.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local Grafo instances and does not persist data, modify static variables, or require cleanup; no @After cleanup is necessary.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class), providing meaningful categorization for selective test execution.
